title: New U.S. Missile Hit Iranian Sports Hall and School, Analysis Shows
partialText: The Pentagon used missiles untested in combat in a deadly attack that struck civilian sites near a military compound on Feb. 28, according to visual evidence examined by The Times and weapons experts.

title: Trump Claims ‘Regime Change’ in Iran Is Already Complete
partialText: President Trump suggested that Iran’s current leaders were “much more reasonable” as he sought to show progress in his war aims. Iran’s power structure appears firmly in control despite a month of U.S.-Israeli attacks.

title: Private-Credit Wobbles Could Prove Perilous for Trump
partialText: The Trump administration is poised to broaden access to risky investments that are showing signs of strain.

title: Justice Dept. Watchdog Has Gone Silent, Lawyers for Whistle-Blower Say
partialText: Lawyers for a fired Justice Department lawyer say the agency’s inspector general appears to have ignored at least 20 different requests to scrutinize misconduct.

title: U.S. Allows Russian Oil Tanker to Reach Cuba, Despite Blockade
partialText: The tanker full of crude oil could reach its expected destination by Monday, providing a lifeline to the island amid intense U.S. pressure.

title: Markwayne Mullin Takes Over DHS With Less Flash but Same Mission
partialText: Markwayne Mullin, the incoming D.H.S. secretary, faces a difficult balance: a public reset of the agency while delivering on President Trump’s deportation agenda.

title: Texas Border Wall Plan in Big Bend Draws Opposition From Republicans and Democrats
partialText: Plans for a wall in Big Bend National Park prompted public protests and behind-the-scenes lobbying to sway the Trump administration to stop.

title: Trump’s Birthright Citizenship Order at Supreme Court Splits Conservative Scholars
partialText: Before President Trump’s order to limit birthright citizenship, there was widespread agreement that the 14th Amendment guaranteed citizenship for U.S.-born babies.

title: Michael Rousseau, Air Canada’s CEO, to Step Down Amid Backlash Over Comments After Crash
partialText: Michael Rousseau’s mostly English statement after a fatal runway collision drew sharp criticism. The airline said it would emphasize French fluency in its search for a successor.

title: What We Know About the T.S.A. and ICE Presence at Airports
partialText: Transportation Security Agency officers have called out of work or quit after weeks of not getting paid during a partial government shutdown. ICE agents have begun to fill their roles.

title: Doctors Believed Woody Brown Would Never Understand Language. He’s Publishing a Novel.
partialText: Doctors believed that Woody Brown would never be able to speak or process language. He went to graduate school and is publishing his debut novel.

title: Who’s ‘Safer’ or ‘Riskier’? Maine Democrats Clash Over How to Beat Collins.
partialText: Gov. Janet Mills argues that her rival for Senate, Graham Platner, could be doomed by his history of offensive online remarks. But at a time of anti-establishment anger, Mr. Platner says he is the safer choice.

title: ‘I Think That MAGA Is Dying:’ Inside the Youth Movement at CPAC
partialText: At a sparsely attended Conservative Political Action Conference, young Republicans were eager to start the post-Trump era.

title: A Democratic Electrician Nabs a State Senate Seat in Republican Florida
partialText: With Brian Nathan’s victory certified, Democrats won two of three state legislative races in this month’s special elections, all in Republican-leaning districts.

title: Israel Debates Law to Allow Hanging of Palestinians Convicted of Deadly Attacks
partialText: The law could apply to Jewish Israeli extremists, but experts say that will likely never happen.

title: Israel Pulls Battalion From West Bank After Soldier Talks of ‘Revenge’
partialText: While detaining a CNN crew, a soldier said that Israeli troops were motivated by “revenge” against Palestinians and that all of the West Bank was “for the Jews.”

title: How to Watch and See the Artemis II Moon Launch
partialText: The first crewed mission around the moon in more than 50 years is coming up. Here’s how to see it at sites in and around the Kennedy Space Center in Florida or online.

title: NASA Is Launching Astronauts to the Moon, but Americans Aren’t That Excited
partialText: Polling has consistently found that most people would prefer NASA spend money on things like monitoring climate change and averting asteroid collisions rather than human spaceflight.

title: How Russia Weaponized the Cold Ukrainian Winter
partialText: Inside one Kyiv neighborhood as it braved the harshest conditions since World War II.

title: The Dogma of Meat
partialText: From Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s food pyramid to online influencers, beef has become more than just a source of protein.

title: How a Civics School With a Conservative Bent Divided Its Supporters
partialText: A University of North Carolina program was intended to promote civil discourse and ideological diversity. Some of its early conservative supporters say it is doing the opposite.

title: How Bard College Became a Major Real Estate Player 20 Miles Away
partialText: A nonprofit foundation donated $82 million worth of properties in Hudson, N.Y., to the school, which has provided few details about its plans.

title: Can You Fake Being Rich?
partialText: A spate of popular social media accounts offer advice on how to achieve an “old-money” look.

title: The Epstein Class Had a Signature Weakness
partialText: Epstein flourished by helping elite men reconcile their private desires with their public appearances.

title: Billionaires, Stop Whining About the Giving Pledge and Try Giving Yourselves
partialText: It makes no sense to me that billionaires would criticize others for trying to help their fellow humans.

title: Your Questions About the News
partialText: Times reporters answer reader questions about the war, the economy and more.

title: They’ve Been Accused of Running a ‘Covert’ Operation in Greenland. It’s No Secret.
partialText: Members of President Trump’s circle, working in plain sight, have caught the eye of Denmark’s intelligence services for trying to make friends and cut deals on the Danish territory.

title: He Led Congo for 18 Years. Now, Joseph Kabila Is a Hunted Man.
partialText: Joseph Kabila, the former president, faces the death penalty after the government convicted him of treason last year. He says the charges are bogus.

title: Renoir, Cézanne and Matisse Paintings Are Stolen in 3-Minute Museum Heist, Police Say
partialText: Thieves broke into the Magnani-Rocca Foundation outside Parma, Italy, officials said, and made off with paintings worth millions.

title: The Founder of a Sexual Liberation Group Is in Jail, but Still Has Fans
partialText: Nicole Daedone, the former leader of OneTaste, is set to be sentenced after being convicted of forced labor conspiracy last year. But she is still finding ways to spread her message from behind bars.
